description: The Science Data Bank deposit inventories 255 debris-flow catchments along National Highway 318 in the China–Nepal transport corridor. The producer team combined remote-sensing identification, field checks, a digital elevation model, geological information and historical weather data. The article describes a debris-flow extent vector file, an inventory vector file and a spreadsheet of catchment attributes. Attributes include outlet coordinates, area, elevation, slope, lithology, fault density, annual precipitation and temperature. The named repository page is public under CC BY 4.0. A road modeller could overlay the mapped catchments with highway links to locate exposure or test disruption scenarios. This is an inventory of identified flows and terrain conditions, not a measured frequency or probability of future debris flows. The article reports field checks, but completeness along each road segment is not established by the summary. The files and coordinate reference system were not inspected by download. The resource is distinct from the Karakoram Highway landslide inventory and the Gilgit-Baltistan susceptibility deposit.
name: A dataset of distributions and characteristics of debris flows in the China-Nepal Traffic Corridor along the 318 National Highway(2022)
